title: Reliability Initiative Matrix (RIM): quantifying rollback thresholds and initiative KPIs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Build a canonical Reliability Initiative Matrix (RIM) to make rollout/rollback decisions for SLO initiatives data-driven. RIM will link initiatives to: measured SLIs, error-budget runway, burn-rate thresholds, owner/cadence, rollout windows, and automated rollback triggers. This ticket covers product definition, acceptance criteria, and integrations with Console dashboards, Alerting (PagerDuty), and the initiative tracker ledger.

acceptance_criteria: RIM UI shows all active reliability initiatives with columns: current SLI, target, error budget remaining (time-based and tokens), burn rate (1h/24h/7d), owner, current rollout fraction, and rollback threshold.
Each initiative row has explicit rollback policy: numeric burn-rate threshold(s), cooldown period, and an owner-defined severity action (pause, rollback, throttle).
Console exposes an API endpoint to fetch initiative status and computed rollback suggestion for programmatic automation.
Automated alerting pipeline surfaces 'rollback recommended' signals to PagerDuty and the initiative owner's Slack channel with a one-click acknowledge action in Console.
Integration tests validate RIM calculations using synthetic traces and match ENG telemetry v2 output within ±5% for burn-rate and error-budget computations.
Rollout experiment: RIM read-only beta enabled for 10 internal teams and collects feedback for 2 cycles before public rollout.
decision_log: 2026-02-28 - Decision: track both short and medium burn rates (1h and 7d) to reduce oscillation during transient traffic spikes.
2026-03-04 - Decision: default policy = conservative for customer-facing models to minimize user-visible degradations; documented override flow for emergency experiments.
2026-03-06 - Decision: RIM will not auto-roll back without owner acknowledgement for P0 initiatives during business hours; automated rollback allowed for P1/P2 with strict cooldown.
